cim: Green Bay considers rules for AI use in public art
cim_eredeti: Green Bay considers rules for AI use in public art
szoveg_eredeti:
GREEN BAY, Wis. — The city of Green Bay is considering new rules for how artificial intelligence can be used in community artwork.

The city has more than 250 pieces of public art, and the collection continues to grow.

Public Arts Coordinator Chelle Diederich said the idea came from staff discussions and inspiration from policies in two municipalities in Idaho.

The Public Arts Commission considered an action to develop a firm policy at its Oct. 28 meeting. Previously, members had no real guidance on how to score submissions that include AI.

“It’s a little bit up to our committee members and our liaisons who are voting on the pieces to vote and to make their interpretations of the rubric,” Diederich said.

The commission voted to research the policy. The plan is in its early phases.

Diederich said the team hopes to eventually conduct a survey to help gauge where lines are on generative AI and AI tool use in city-funded art.

“My hope is that it supports our mission as the Public Arts Commission, gives support for artists in this community, and artists throughout our range of who we work with, but also gives confidence to our commission members, our liaisons, who are voting,” Diederich said.

With public input from the survey, city staff are expected to bring the issue back to the Public Arts Commission in January.
